# Media Puppies

> Paid media team for agencies and businesses in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.
> We run Google Ads and Meta (Facebook and Instagram) ads as a white label partner for marketing agencies,
> and as a dedicated media buyer for brands. The team is based in Noida, India, so account work and
> reporting happen while US and UK clients sleep. Month to month, no lock-in, never a percentage of ad spend.

Updated 2026-11-06. 242 articles, 28 free calculators, 72 service and market pages.

## Key facts

- Services: white label PPC and paid social for agencies; dedicated media buyer; Google Ads; Meta ads; LinkedIn ads; SEO; AI automation.
- Markets served: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, United Arab Emirates and India.
- Team location: Noida, Delhi NCR, India. Invoiced to clients in their own currency.
- Pricing model: a fixed monthly fee per account, month to month. Never a percentage of ad spend. The fee depends on the account and is given on the first call, after an audit.
- White label terms: mutual NDA and non-solicit before access; the end client's ad accounts stay in the client's name; reporting in the agency's own template.
- First step for a new account: a written audit within two working days of access.
- Contact: info@mediapuppies.com

## Original research (our own data, free to cite with a link)

Hub: https://mediapuppies.com/research/

- [What do real estate leads cost in 2026? Zillow's new fee, and the Facebook, Google and ChatGPT numbers agents showed on YouTube](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/real-estate-leads-cost/): Zillow is moving its buyer leads to Zillow Preferred, where agents pay nothing upfront and hand over 15% to 40% of their commission at closing. Two-thirds of buyer connections went to Preferred agents in Q3 2026, and Zillow expects 100% in the first half of 2027. An Orange County agent who spent about nine months on Zillow Flex says Flex agents pay Zillow 40% at closing, and agents on his team kept 25% of the commission. A Maryland agent got 10 deals from Zillow; one neighbourhood cost him almost $1,600 a month, where a closing may pay $13,000 or more. The real Facebook lead costs shown ran from $4 to $10. One Texas campaign spent $2,184 for 283 leads at $7.72 each, and its first closing, worth $10,710 in commission, came in month five. A Toronto team leader paid an agency while his cost per lead climbed to about $80. His own campaigns now get leads at $4 to $6. An Austin agent spent $1,300 on ChatGPT ads for 13 seller leads, about $100 each, at a $63 cost per 1,000 impressions. We screened 69 videos: 36 were more than a year old, and only 14 of the 30 recent ones gave a number we could use. 50% of the 104 numbers came from a real account.
- [What do Angi leads cost in 2026? 214 numbers from 25 YouTube videos on Angi, Thumbtack and Google LSA](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/angi-leads-cost/): We screened 70 YouTube videos and kept 25 uploaded between 5 November 2025 and 28 October 2026 that state concrete lead numbers for Angi, Thumbtack or Google Local Services Ads: 214 numbers, 183 of them about these platforms or lead marketplaces in general. Only two videos showed real Angi spend. An HVAC company in Ontario paid $80 a lead (the video does not say which dollars) for 60 leads and closed 3 jobs, $1,600 per job. An electrician in Louisiana turned one $24 lead into about $66,000 of work. On Angi's May 2026 earnings call, CEO Jeff Kip said pros pay $50 a lead, win 1 in 7 or 1 in 8, and the average job is about $4,000. Angi's Q1 2026 release reported 105,000 average monthly active US pros, down 22% in a year. Videos claimed a marketplace lead goes to as many as 10 other contractors. Angi's own help pages cap each request at five pros, and Thumbtack limits a customer to five pros in the first four hours. On a podcast about Google Local Services Ads, Sam Preston of the agency Service Scalers read out cost per lead a year apart: roofing $74 to $107, electrical $29 to $43, plumbing $70 to $66. He did not say whether these were LSA only. Only 24.8% of the numbers came from a real account, and 27.6% were worked examples. For Thumbtack it was 1 of 21, and 7 more were prices on one owner's screen.
- [AI Overviews on the searches advertisers pay for: 339 US Google Ads keywords, 118 of them also checked in the UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/ai-overviews-ads-study/): On 3 November 2026 Google showed an AI Overview on 196 of 339 US searches that advertisers pay for (57.8%). Leaving out "near me" searches, it was 175 of 278 (62.9%). Cost questions almost always got one: 33 of 36 (91.7%), and all 33 of those AI Overviews quoted dollar figures. The priciest clicks were not spared. With near-me searches left out, keywords with an estimated CPC of $30 or more showed an AI Overview 62.5% of the time, against 63.1% below $30. Cheaper keywords got more overall, mostly because cheap cost questions almost always get one. With near-me searches left out, every insurance and software keyword showed an AI Overview. Home service searches other than cost questions showed one only 39.1% of the time, and legal searches 44.8%. At least 128 of the 196 US AI Overviews (65.3%) asked the searcher a question, such as their city, budget or loan amount. Among the 135 we captured in full, 128 did (94.8%). On 95 searches run in all four countries the rates were close: Australia 80%, Canada 74.7%, the UK 73.7% and the US 72.6%. With a single run, that order could easily change.
- [How much do Facebook ads cost in 2026? 212 numbers from 29 YouTube videos by ad buyers and marketers](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ads-cost/): We screened 69 YouTube videos and kept 29 uploaded between November 2025 and November 2026 that state concrete Facebook ad costs, 212 numbers in all. Where a country was named it was the US, UK or Australia. Eight videos reported a real cost per lead. Four fell between $7.72 and $21.80, and the range ran from $1 to $2 for a free B2B guide to a roofing campaign that started at $25 and rose past $50. None of the 9 CPM figures came from a real ad account, and 7 were worked examples. The only cited average was $8.15. WordStream and LocalIQ's 2026 report on 452 US lead campaigns put the median cost per lead at $27.39, with real estate at $13.74 and home improvement at $42.95. Seven channels named a starting budget, from $10 to $100 a day, with a median of $35. In case-study videos 79.3% of the numbers came from a real account. In cost, budget and how-to videos it was 20%, and 37.5% were worked examples.
- [Dental marketing in 2026: what patient clicks cost on Google, and what 99 advertisers run on Facebook](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/dental-marketing-data/): Across 37 US patient keywords, the median Google cost per click was $6.39. Implants and dentures had the highest group median at $10.26, driven by implants. For treatment searches, adding "near me" raised the click price sharply: by 82% for dental implants and 130% for Invisalign. For general searches such as "dentist" it barely moved. Price searches were cheaper than the treatment itself in all 5 pairs with an estimate, for example $3.23 for "invisalign cost" against $4.68 for "invisalign". One implant chain ran 73 of the 192 live dental ads on Facebook and Instagram. Across the other 98 advertisers' 119 ads, single images led at 42% and video was 26.9%. 71.4% of those 119 ads had been running for a year or more, and the median ad had been live for 456 days.
- [Facebook Ad Library study: what 673 live US ads from law firms, dentists, real estate and home services show](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ad-library-study/): On 3 November 2026 the median active ad had already been live for 271 days, and 42.6% of the 673 ads had been running for a year or more. 79.6% of the 427 advertisers had exactly one active ad. In real estate the figure was 92%. Formats split by trade: 37% of law firm ads were video, against 11.1% for home services, where 52.1% were single images. 28.7% of law firm ads offered something free, usually a consultation, and 21.4% of home service ads offered a free estimate or inspection. Of 99 real estate ads aimed at buyers, sellers or renters, 88.9% carried Meta's Housing label. 11 did not.
- [How much does Google Ads cost for home services? We priced 169 keywords in 8 trades.](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-ads-cost-home-services/): Across 169 US home service keywords, the median Google Ads cost per click was $17.62, and the middle half ran from $7.73 to $25.63. Water damage had the priciest clicks (median $33.84) and locksmith the cheapest ($5.80). The most expensive single keyword was emergency water damage restoration at $66.23. Emergency searches had a median CPC of $27.91: 1.36 times repair searches and 4.49 times price-research searches. Adding "near me" made no consistent difference. It raised the CPC in 9 of 17 keyword pairs, by a median of $0.21. Install and replacement keywords cost a median $13.05 a click, against $20.45 for repair keywords.
- [Law firm marketing in 2026: what Google clicks cost by practice area, and what 146 firms run on Facebook](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/law-firm-marketing-data/): Personal injury keywords had a median US Google cost per click of $156, 16.08 times the median for the other practice areas we checked ($9.70). The priciest keyword we checked was truck accident lawyer, at an estimated $252.78 a click. All eight of the most expensive keywords were injury searches. The "near me" version had a lower CPC estimate in 4 of the 5 legal keyword pairs we compared. On Facebook and Instagram, the median live law firm ad had been running for 181 days, and 28.7% offered something free, such as a consultation or case review. 10.6% of law firm ads were in Spanish or bilingual, and 22 of those 28 were immigration ads.
- [We analysed 439 live US med spa ads in the Meta Ad Library. Here is what they run.](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/med-spa-meta-ads-study/): 80.1% of the 296 med spa advertisers we found had exactly one active ad. Only 2.7% were running five or more. The median med spa ad had been live for 160 days, and 69% had been running for 90 days or longer. 60.1% of ads mentioned a price or a discount, and 28.7% were built around a new-client special. Book now was the most common button, on 32.6% of ads. 53.3% sent people to the clinic's own website. Of 180 ads for Botox-type treatments, 83.9% named a brand such as Botox or Dysport in the copy.
- [Real estate marketing in 2026: the median seller click costs 16 times a buyer click, and what 87 advertisers run on Facebook](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/real-estate-marketing-data/): Our six seller searches had a median US Google cost per click of $25.41, about 16 times the $1.61 median for six buyer searches. Sell-now searches drove it; value checks cost under $3. "Sell my house" was estimated at $69.29 a click and "we buy houses" $40.68, while "homes for sale" was $0.48. Searches for an agent cost from $7.30 ("realtor near me") to $13.21 ("listing agent"); the five in our agents group had a median of $8. In our Facebook Ad Library sample, 92% of the 87 real estate advertisers appeared with just one ad, and the median ad had been running for 347 days. 88.9% of the 99 consumer real estate ads carried Meta's Housing label, and 19.2% were catalog ads built from a listing feed.
- [What is CPC? Cost per click explained, with Google Ads CPC estimates for 339 US keywords across 11 industries](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/what-is-cpc/): Across 339 US keywords in 11 industries, the median estimated Google Ads cost per click was $12.32, pulled up by 169 home service keywords. The median of the 11 industry medians was $9.47. Among our samples, insurance had the highest industry median at $35.44 (4 of its 10 keywords were quote searches) and ecommerce the lowest at $2.08, about 17 times lower. 12 keywords cost $100 or more per click: 11 personal injury searches and google ads management at $228.10. Insurance searches asking for a quote had a median of $71.04 across 4 keywords, against $19.14 for 6 other insurance searches. The four cheapest clicks were home-buying and rental searches: condos for sale was estimated at $0.34 a click.

- [LinkedIn Ads Agency](https://mediapuppies.com/linkedin-ads-agency/): LinkedIn advertising for B2B brands with high contract values. Account-based targeting, Conversions API, and when LinkedIn is too expensive.

- [SaaS Performance Marketing Agency](https://mediapuppies.com/saas-performance-marketing-agency/): Paid acquisition for B2B and product-led SaaS. Optimised to qualified pipeline and payback period using offline conversion import, not to form fills.
- [B2B Lead Generation Agency](https://mediapuppies.com/b2b-lead-generation-agency/): B2B paid media that is judged on qualified pipeline, not form fills. Google search, LinkedIn and Meta, with CRM outcomes fed back into the bidding.
- [Home Services Lead Generation](https://mediapuppies.com/home-services-lead-generation/): Paid media for home services: HVAC, roofing, plumbing, solar, remodelling. Call tracking, service-area structure and Local Services Ads, judged on booked jobs.
- [Performance Marketing Agency in India](https://mediapuppies.com/performance-marketing/): Performance marketing agency in India running Meta and Google ads for D2C brands and lead-gen businesses, reported in cost per customer. Month to month.

## Reading for US, UK, Canadian and Australian buyers

- [White label PPC: how it works, what it costs agencies and where it goes wrong](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-ppc-how-it-works/): White label PPC explained: how agencies resell Google and Meta ads under their own brand, how partners are priced, what can go wrong and how to start safely.
- [White label Facebook ads: how agencies resell Meta ads without the headaches](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-facebook-ads/): White label Facebook ads let an agency sell Meta advertising under its own brand while a partner runs the accounts. How it works, pricing models and the risks.
- [Eight questions to ask a white label partner before you send an account](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-partner-questions/): Eight questions for a white label partner before you send the first account: staffing, scope, reporting, pricing, and what they will refuse to do.
- [White label PPC pricing: how partners bill and where the margin goes](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-ppc-pricing/): White label PPC pricing comes in three shapes, each changing who carries the risk. How partners bill, what is excluded, and how to price it on to clients.
- [White label reporting: how to build white label reports clients trust](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-reporting/): White label reporting explained: what belongs in white label reports, a monthly workflow, the best tools, where reports leak and who writes the commentary.
- [Outsource PPC management: when it makes sense and how to do it safely](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/outsource-ppc-management/): When to outsource PPC, what an outsourced PPC team should handle, how to compare agencies, freelancers and offshore teams, and how to keep control.
- [How to outsource digital marketing without losing control of it](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/outsource-digital-marketing/): How to outsource digital marketing: which parts to hand over, which to keep in-house, how to choose a partner, and how to run it so results stay visible.
- [Building an offshore marketing team: agency, dedicated hire or staff augmentation](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/offshore-marketing-team/): An offshore marketing team adds senior skills at a different cost base. The three ways to build one, roles to start with, and managing across time zones.
- [Working with an offshore media buyer: the only number that matters](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/offshore-media-buyer-overlap/): Hiring an offshore media buyer: the overlap hours that decide whether it works, what each band feels like, and what to ask before you commit.
- [When an agency should outsource media buying instead of hiring](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/when-to-outsource-media-buying/): When to outsource media buying rather than hire: the arithmetic that decides it, the four signals you have already waited too long, and the option nobody takes.
- [Hiring an Indian marketing agency from the US: what changes](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/indian-marketing-agency-us/): What a US business should settle before hiring an Indian marketing agency: the overlap problem, special ad categories, privacy law, contracts and payment.
- [Hiring an Indian marketing agency from the UK: how it actually works](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/indian-marketing-agency-uk/): What changes when a UK business hires an Indian marketing agency — overlap hours, contracts, payment, data protection, and the regulatory knowledge to test for.
- [Paying an Indian agency from overseas: invoices, FX and tax](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/paying-an-indian-agency/): The mechanics of paying an Indian agency from abroad: invoicing currency, GST on exported services, transfer routes, and who absorbs the bank fees.
- [Planning for Q4 in the US: what actually happens to costs](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/us-q4-ad-costs-planning/): Q4 ad costs in the US climb from October, peak around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, and fall in January. How to budget for it rather than react.
- [Why your US conversions fell and nobody changed anything](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/us-state-privacy-consent-conversions/): US state privacy laws, Global Privacy Control and consent mode quietly cut the conversion data reaching Meta and Google. How to tell if it is you.
- [Lead forms that will actually be followed up: US consent wording](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/us-lead-form-consent-language/): If your US leads will be called or texted, the lead form consent wording next to the submit button matters. What belongs on it, and who writes it.
- [Special Ad Categories: why your US targeting disappeared](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/meta-special-ad-categories-us/): Housing, employment, credit and social issues strip most Meta targeting in the US. What special ad categories remove, what stays, and how to adapt.
- [Local Services Ads: the US listing above your search ads](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-local-services-ads-us/): How Google Local Services Ads work for US home service firms in 2026: lead costs by trade, the move into Google Ads, missed-call charges and verification.
- [PECR, consent mode, and the UK conversions you stopped seeing](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/uk-consent-mode-conversion-loss/): UK cookie consent is governed by PECR, and how consent mode is wired decides how much data reaches Meta and Google. How to diagnose a sudden drop.
- [The UK retail calendar: planning around Black Friday and Boxing Day](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/uk-retail-seasonality-planning/): UK retail seasonality has two peaks rather than one, and January behaves differently here than elsewhere. How to budget for the real shape of the year.
- [Financial promotions in the UK: the rule that stops campaigns dead](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/fca-financial-promotions-paid-media/): Promoting an investment, credit product or crypto to UK consumers means the financial promotions rules apply. What that does to a paid media plan.
- [Advertising in Canada: what Indian export brands should know](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/advertising-in-canada/): Advertising in Canada looks like the US and is not. Bilingual requirements, anti-spam law, provincial privacy rules and a thinner auction all change the plan.
- [Why 30 June is Australia’s biggest month and your calendar missed it](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/australia-eofy-marketing/): EOFY marketing in Australia: why the run-up to 30 June is a real demand spike for anything a business can expense, and how to plan ads around it.
